_comment: Manual overrides per species, keyed by scientific name: {"include": [inat photo ids, forced in first, in this order], "exclude": [inat photo ids never chosen], "description": {"summary", "field_marks", "size", "habitat": text written over the Wikipedia-derived fields}, "limit": N cleared candidates to consider instead of the build's --limit, "trust_article": true to take a Wikipedia article whose lead names neither the BirdNET binomial nor the BirdNET common name, "sounds": {"song": "xc-<nr>", "call": "xc-<nr>" pinned first, "exclude": [recording ids never chosen], "xeno_canto_name": the name xeno-canto files the species under, "accept": [species BirdNET may hear instead, the other half of a split]}}. Photo ids are in the pack's report.json and LICENSE.

Pyrocephalus rubinus._why: BirdNET calls it Scarlet Flycatcher, Pyrocephalus rubinus; Wikipedia's Vermilion flycatcher article is Pyrocephalus obscurus after the split, and is the right bird here

Anas platyrhynchos._why: most desert-park 'Mallards' are domestic breeds; 200 candidates find wild ones; excluded: a buff domestic duck; a white domestic duck; a dark domestic duck; white domestic runner ducks

Lanius ludovicianus._why: excluded: not a shrike on the card

Junco hyemalis._why: excluded: no bird visible in the crop

Phalaenoptilus nuttallii._why: excluded: held in a gloved hand; held in a hand

Rallus limicola._why: excluded: held in a gloved hand

Anas crecca._why: excluded: dead on a deck; a distant flock

Setophaga aestiva._why: BirdNET+ carries both halves of the yellow warbler split and hears American recordings as Setophaga petechia (#41)
